title: Predicting Student Retention Using Machine Learning: A Philippine Higher Education Case Study
authors: Delena, M. T.; Fernandez, A.; Santos, J. R.
venue: Journal of Computational Research and Technology
tldr: Develops an ensemble ML model (Random Forest + XGBoost) for predicting student retention at a Philippine university, achieving 94.2% accuracy, with academic performance and financial aid status as top predictors.
problem_and_motivation: Student attrition is a significant challenge for Philippine universities, but existing retention prediction models are developed in Western contexts and may not transfer to Philippine higher education due to different socioeconomic factors (e.g., remittances, informal financial support).
approach: Dataset: 8,542 student records from a Philippine university spanning 2018-2023 academic years.
Features: 28 variables including demographics, academic performance (GPA, units enrolled), financial indicators (scholarship status, family income bracket, payment history), and engagement metrics.
Preprocessing: handling missing values (mean/median imputation), outlier detection, SMOTE for class imbalance (retention rate 72%).
Feature selection: Recursive Feature Elimination with Cross-Validation (RFECV).
Models tested: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost, and ensemble (RF+XGBoost stacking).
Evaluation: 5-fold cross-validation with accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, AUC-ROC.
findings: num: Ensemble model (RF + XGBoost) achieved 94.2% accuracy, 0.96 AUC-ROC for retention prediction.
Top predictors: cumulative GPA (feature importance 0.31), financial aid status (0.18), attendance rate (0.15), family income (0.12).
Ensemble outperformed individual RF (92.1%) and XGBoost (91.8%) models.
Financial aid status had higher predictive power in the Philippine model compared to Western literature benchmarks.
Students from lowest income bracket have 3.2x higher attrition risk than highest bracket.
SHAP analysis showed tuition payment delays (>=2 months) as a key risk indicator.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Demonstrates the application of ensemble ML with SHAP explainability in a Philippine educational context. The finding that financial aid has higher predictive power in the Philippines vs. Western contexts highlights the importance of localized ML models. The methodology (ensemble stacking, RFECV, SMOTE, SHAP) is directly transferable to PFMS prediction tasks.
directly_justifies: Ensemble (RF+XGBoost stacking) outperforms individual models for prediction tasks.
SHAP analysis identifies key financial risk indicators (tuition payment delays).
Financial features have context-dependent predictive power needing localization.
limits: Applied to student retention, not PFMS. [acknowledged]
No real-time deployment or prediction pipeline evaluation. [unacknowledged]
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains was performed. Domain 14.A was flagged as high relevance for the ensemble ML approach, feature selection methodology, and SHAP explainability. Domain 5.A was flagged as medium relevance because socioeconomic features are used for profiling. Domains 1-4, 6-13, 14.B were rejected as the paper addresses student retention prediction, not personal finance or PFMS.
